name: Fixed-effects (common-effect) model
variables: y_i = observed effect size in study i; beta_F = common population effect shared by all k studies; e_i = sampling error; v_i = known sampling variance of study i
notes: Model statement; engine call model='fixed'. Observed differences between studies are attributed mainly to sampling error.

name: Inverse-variance weight
variables: w_i = weight (precision) of study i; v_i = sampling variance of study i
notes: The source calls w_i the weight and precision. Under random effects the engine uses 1/(v_i + tau^2), which the source does not print.

name: Fixed-effects pooled estimate
variables: beta_F_hat = estimated common effect; w_i = 1/v_i; y_i = effect size of study i; k = number of studies
notes: Engine call model='fixed' (ci_method defaults to 'z'). Its standard error, SE = 1/sqrt(sum w_i), is the standard companion result but is NOT printed in the source; the engine returns it as se_wald.

name: Cochran's Q statistic
variables: w_i = 1/v_i; y_i = effect size of study i; beta_F_hat = fixed-effects pooled estimate; k = number of studies
notes: Uses fixed-effects weights. The source warns Q has low power with few studies and is usually significant with many; do not choose FE vs RE from it.

name: Q test of homogeneity
expression: Q ~ chi2(df = k - 1) under H0;  p = P(chi2_{k-1} >= Q);  reject homogeneity if p < alpha = .05
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; df = degrees of freedom; alpha = significance level
notes: Engine returns p_Q (via distributions.chi2_sf). Worked example: chi2(49) = 85.71, p < .001; exact p is about 0.00092 (computed, not printed). [note: because of the low power of Q, Cochrane Handbook v6 suggests alpha = 0.10; a non-significant Q does not show homogeneity, and the test must not decide FE vs RE.]

name: Random-effects model
expression: y_i = beta_R + u_i + e_i,  Var(u_i) = tau^2,  Var(e_i) = v_i
variables: y_i = observed effect size; beta_R = average population effect; u_i = study-specific deviation of the population effect; tau^2 = between-study (population heterogeneity) variance; e_i = sampling error; v_i = sampling variance
notes: Engine call model='random'. The source names no tau^2 estimator; its results come from metaSEM, whose meta() uses ML (external knowledge). To mimic: tau2_method='ML', ci_method='z'. Engine defaults are REML and HKSJ. [note: Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML or Paule-Mandel over DerSimonian-Laird for tau^2 and suggests considering HKSJ intervals.]

name: Mixed-effects meta-regression
expression: y_i = beta_0 + beta_1 * x_i + u_i + e_i,  Var(u_i) = tau^2 (residual)
variables: y_i = effect size of study i; x_i = study characteristic (moderator) of study i; beta_0 = intercept; beta_1 = regression coefficient; u_i = residual random effect; tau^2 = residual heterogeneity after controlling for x_i; e_i = sampling error with Var(e_i) = v_i
notes: Typo in the source: Eq. (4) prints 'beta_1 x_1' while the text defines x_i. Interpret at the study level only (ecological fallacy). Worked example: slope for mean age -0.0071 (95% CI -0.0128; -0.0014). Engine reproduction of the source: meta_regression(..., tau2_method='ML', test='z'). [note: Cochrane Handbook v6 asks for pre-specified moderators (about 10 studies per moderator) and recommends Knapp-Hartung inference (engine test='knha').]

name: I-squared from tau^2 and typical within-study variance (Higgins & Thompson 2002 definition)
variables: tau_hat^2 = estimated between-study variance (model estimate, ML in metaSEM); v_typical = typical within-study variance (see the typical within-study variance formula)
notes: NOT printed in the source: reconstructed in the extraction notes because the reported I^2 = .3955 does not equal (Q - df)/Q = .4283. Implied v_typical = tau^2(1 - I^2)/I^2 = 0.0273*0.6045/0.3955, about 0.0417. Engine returns it in percent as I2_from_tau2 when tau^2 is supplied; the source reports a proportion.

name: Typical within-study variance
variables: k = number of studies; w_i = 1/v_i
notes: Not printed in the source; from the extraction-note reconstruction of metaSEM's I^2. Engine returns it as s2_typical.

name: I-squared from Q (contrast variant)
expression: I^2 = max(0, (Q - df) / Q),  df = k - 1
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1; k = number of studies
notes: Not printed in the source; computed in the extraction notes only to show the mismatch: (85.71 - 49)/85.71 = .4283 vs reported .3955. Engine's default I2 field uses this variant, in percent.

name: Log relative risk
variables: a = successes in group 1; b = failures in group 1; n1 = a + b; c = successes in group 2; d = failures in group 2; n2 = c + d; log = natural logarithm
notes: Undefined if a or c is 0; the source mentions no continuity correction. Engine measure 'RR' adds 0.5 to all cells when any cell is 0 (cc_to='only0') and drops double-zero studies by default.

name: Sampling variance of the log relative risk
variables: a, c = successes in groups 1 and 2; n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: SE = sqrt(v_RR).

name: Log odds ratio
variables: a, b = successes and failures in group 1; c, d = successes and failures in group 2; log = natural logarithm
notes: Undefined if any cell is 0; no continuity correction in the source. Engine measure 'OR'.

name: Sampling variance of the log odds ratio
variables: a, b, c, d = the four cell counts of the 2x2 table
notes: Woolf variance. SE = sqrt(v_OR).

name: Pooled within-group variance
variables: S1^2, S2^2 = sample variances of groups 1 and 2; n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: Engine returns the square root (S_pooled).

name: Raw (unstandardized) mean difference
variables: X1_bar, X2_bar = sample means of groups 1 and 2
notes: Suitable when the scale is meaningful across studies (e.g. blood pressure, heart rate, IQ).

name: Sampling variance of the raw mean difference (pooled)
variables: S2_pooled = pooled within-group variance; n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: Assumes equal group variances. Engine: effect_sizes.md(vtype='pooled') (`--md-vtype pooled`); the default effect_sizes.md uses the unpooled S1^2/n1 + S2^2/n2, and the two agree only when n1 = n2.

name: Standardized mean difference (Hedges' g, approximate correction)
variables: X1_bar, X2_bar = group means; S_pooled = sqrt(S2_pooled); n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: Engine: smd(..., correct=True, j_method='approx'); the engine default j_method='exact' uses the gamma-function J and gives a slightly different g. In the illustration the SMD is schizophrenia minus control (expected negative).

name: Hedges' small-sample correction factor (approximation)
variables: df = degrees of freedom of the pooled SD; n1, n2 = group sizes
notes: Engine: hedges_j(df, method='approx'). Identity check: 4(n1+n2-2) - 1 = 4(n1+n2) - 9.

name: Sampling variance of the SMD
variables: n1, n2 = group sizes; y_SMD = bias-corrected SMD (Hedges' g)
notes: Plugs the corrected g in directly; no J^2 multiplication; denominator 2(n1+n2), not 2(n1+n2-2) or 2(n1+n2-3.94). Equals metafor's 'LS' variance and engine vtype='LS'. State the variant, because other textbooks differ in the 3rd-4th decimal.

name: Correlation coefficient as effect size
variables: r = sample correlation coefficient
notes: Engine measure 'COR'. Schmidt & Hunter pool raw r (with artifact corrections).

name: Sampling variance of r
variables: r = sample correlation; n = sample size
notes: Depends on r itself, which is one reason Hedges & Olkin prefer Fisher's z.

name: Fisher's z transformation
variables: r = sample correlation; log = natural logarithm
notes: Engine measure 'ZCOR' (atanh). No back-transformation is given in the source; r = tanh(z) via effect_sizes.back_transform.

name: Sampling variance of Fisher's z
variables: n = sample size
notes: Independent of r; requires n > 3.

name: Wald (z-based) 95% confidence interval
variables: estimate = pooled effect or regression coefficient; SE = its standard error
locator: p. 126 (inferred from the symmetric reported CIs)
notes: Not stated in the source: the reported CIs are symmetric, consistent with Wald z intervals (metaSEM default). Engine: ci_method='z'. Example: -0.7287 (-0.8019; -0.6555). [note: Wald z intervals for a random-effects mean are too narrow when k is small; Cochrane Handbook v6 suggests considering HKSJ (engine default ci_method='hksj').]

name: Standard error back-calculated from a symmetric 95% CI
expression: SE = (upper - lower) / (2 * 1.96);  midpoint check: estimate = (lower + upper) / 2
variables: upper, lower = 95% confidence limits; 1.96 = standard normal 97.5th percentile
notes: Reviewer check from the extraction notes. Illustration: (-0.6555 - (-0.8019))/(2*1.96) gives SE about 0.0373 and the midpoint equals -0.7287; slope CI gives SE about 0.0029 with midpoint -0.0071. Also useful at S05 for extracting variances from reported CIs.
